summary: Hiker stranded overnight in snowstorm on a 13,000-ft ridge north of Mount Princeton; found severely hypothermic, buried in snow in an avalanche chute east of Cottonwood Lake; 3+ hours of active warming, walked to ambulance ~7am
location: 13,000-foot ridge north of Mount Princeton; avalanche chute east of Cottonwood Lake
notes: Merged forum + CCSAR-N news reports (parts: forum, sarlogs-a); found ~2am Nov 9 covered in snow; coded injury (hypothermia) per index convention MERGED (run 59): MRA Meridian Spring 2024 cover story 'Unprepared and Freezing' recounts this Nov 8, 2023 CCSAR deployment: 911 call ~7 p.m., no GPS obtainable from the call; 2 dozen+ CCSAR volunteers searched avalanche chutes in steep terrain and harsh weather, followed footprints >1.5 hrs and found the hiker as an 'unusual looking rock' in new snow, sitting fetal and snow-covered, wearing only a cotton hoodie with no means of rewarming; subject had recent back surgery and was not wearing hearing aids; 3 hrs rewarming, rope-system lower through new snow and over fallen trees, then subject walked out; reached base and ambulance at 7 a.m. Nov 9. MERGED (run 258): advnture.com account of the same Nov 8, 2023 CCSAR deployment — distress call ~7 p.m.; ~25 CCSAR members searched avalanche chutes in 6-8in of new snow; footprints located ~12:42 a.m., subject found ~2 a.m. Nov 9 sitting upright in a fetal position covered in snow (initially mistaken for a rock); severe hypothermia; rope-assisted descent. | 2026-09-15: 14ers.com link removed per site ban; row retains other verified source(s). Run 794: merged HotRR corroborating URL.
